item_description: A former CIA officer who passed classified information to the Soviet Union and Russia.
item_facts: Ames worked in the CIA’s Directorate of Operations.
He was arrested in 1994 and later pleaded guilty to espionage.
His disclosures compromised U.S. intelligence sources and operations.
needs_review: Verify dates, role and impact using court records and declassified official histories.

item_description: A Russian intelligence operative expelled from the United States in 2010 as part of a spy swap.
item_facts: Chapman was one of ten Russian agents arrested in the U.S. in 2010.
She pleaded guilty to conspiracy to act as an unregistered agent of a foreign government.
The group was exchanged for four people imprisoned in Russia.
needs_review: Verify legal wording and exchange details using U.S. court and government records.

item_description: An American convicted of selling classified satellite intelligence to the Soviet Union in the 1970s.
item_facts: Boyce worked at a defense contractor handling classified communications material.
He was convicted of espionage in 1977.
His case inspired the book and film The Falcon and the Snowman.
needs_review: Verify case details and avoid relying on dramatized film depictions.

item_description: A Serbian double agent who supplied intelligence to Britain during World War II while maintaining contact with German intelligence.
item_facts: Popov operated under the British codename Tricycle.
He was part of the Double-Cross System run by British intelligence.
Claims that he directly inspired James Bond are disputed and should be treated cautiously.
needs_review: The Bond inspiration story is contested; verify operational details through archival histories.

item_description: An Israeli intelligence agent who infiltrated Syrian political and military circles in the early 1960s.
item_facts: Cohen operated in Syria under a false identity.
He was arrested by Syrian authorities in 1965.
He was executed in Damascus that year.
needs_review: Verify chronology and reported intelligence impact with archival Israeli and Syrian sources.

item_description: The codename for Spanish double agent Joan Pujol García, who helped deceive German intelligence during World War II.
item_facts: Pujol worked for British intelligence under the codename Garbo.
His network fed false information to German intelligence.
The deception contributed to Allied efforts to mislead Germany about the Normandy invasion.
needs_review: Verify operational details and degree of impact with British archival histories.

item_description: A British intelligence officer who secretly worked for Soviet intelligence during the Cold War.
item_facts: Blake was a member of MI6.
He was convicted of espionage in 1961 and sentenced to 42 years in prison.
He escaped from prison in 1966 and later lived in the Soviet Union and Russia.
needs_review: Verify dates, conviction and escape details against court and archival records.

item_description: A Spanish civilian who became a British double agent under the codename Garbo during World War II.
item_facts: Pujol volunteered to work against Nazi Germany before securing British sponsorship.
His fabricated agent network helped channel deceptive intelligence.
He received the British MBE after the war under his alias.
needs_review: Verify award details and wartime activities using archival British records.

item_description: A senior British intelligence officer who secretly served the Soviet Union as part of the Cambridge spy network.
item_facts: Philby worked for MI6 and rose to a senior position.
He defected to the Soviet Union in 1963.
He was one of the Cambridge Five, a group recruited by Soviet intelligence while at Cambridge.
needs_review: Verify intelligence history and the group’s membership using declassified and scholarly sources.

item_description: A German-born physicist who passed information about the Manhattan Project to the Soviet Union.
item_facts: Fuchs worked on the Manhattan Project in the United States and Britain.
He confessed to espionage in 1950 and was convicted in the UK.
After serving a prison sentence, he moved to East Germany.
needs_review: Verify details using court records and historical archives; distinguish evidence from later claims.

item_description: The stage name of Dutch dancer Margaretha Zelle, executed by France during World War I after conviction for espionage.
item_facts: Zelle was a Dutch citizen and performer in Europe.
A French military court convicted her of aiding Germany in 1917.
Historians have questioned the strength of the evidence and her actual intelligence value.
needs_review: Espionage allegations and evidentiary record are disputed; avoid presenting guilt or impact as settled fact.

item_description: A British civil servant who passed information about atomic research to the Soviet Union over several decades.
item_facts: Norwood worked at the British Non-Ferrous Metals Research Association.
She was identified publicly in 1999 after the release of Soviet intelligence material.
She was never prosecuted.
needs_review: Verify identification and intelligence claims using archival records and reliable histories.

item_description: A New Zealand-born resistance operative who worked with Allied special operations in occupied France during World War II.
item_facts: Wake served with the British Special Operations Executive.
She helped the French Resistance in 1944.
She received multiple Allied decorations for wartime service.
needs_review: Verify operational claims and awards through official military records and reliable biographies.

item_description: A British SOE wireless operator of Indian Muslim heritage who served in occupied France during World War II.
item_facts: Khan was sent to France as a radio operator in 1943.
She continued transmitting after much of her network was compromised.
She was executed at Dachau concentration camp in 1944.
needs_review: Verify biography and operational timeline using official archives and memorial sources.

item_description: A Soviet military intelligence officer who supplied information to Britain and the United States during the Cold War.
item_facts: Penkovsky was arrested in Moscow in 1962.
He was tried and executed in 1963.
His intelligence helped Western governments assess Soviet military capabilities during the Cuban Missile Crisis period.
needs_review: Extent and impact of intelligence are debated; verify against declassified records and scholarly work.

item_description: A German journalist and Soviet intelligence officer who ran a spy network in Japan before and during World War II.
item_facts: Sorge operated in Tokyo under journalistic cover.
Japanese authorities arrested him in 1941.
He was executed in Japan in 1944.
needs_review: Verify operational reporting and its strategic impact using archival historical sources.

item_description: An FBI agent who spied for the Soviet Union and Russia, compromising U.S. intelligence operations.
item_facts: Hanssen was arrested in 2001.
He pleaded guilty to espionage and received a life sentence without parole.
His espionage spanned multiple years and caused serious damage to U.S. intelligence.

item_description: A secret agent active around the turn of the twentieth century whose life became surrounded by legend and embellishment.
item_facts: Reilly worked with British intelligence, though accounts of his exact role vary.
He was involved in operations in Russia during the revolutionary period.
Many dramatic stories about him came from later biographies and popular fiction.
needs_review: High uncertainty: separate documented service from disputed or fictionalized claims.

item_description: A group of British men recruited by Soviet intelligence while studying or working at Cambridge, who later held influential positions.
item_facts: The commonly identified members are Kim Philby, Guy Burgess, Donald Maclean, Anthony Blunt and John Cairncross.
They passed information to the Soviet Union over different periods.
The extent of each member’s activity and the group’s coordination varied.
needs_review: Membership and claims vary in some accounts; verify through declassified records and scholarship.

item_description: An American who served as an Allied agent in occupied France and helped organize resistance networks during World War II.
item_facts: Hall worked for the British Special Operations Executive and later the U.S. Office of Strategic Services.
She operated in France under German occupation.
She received the Distinguished Service Cross, one of few civilian women to do so during World War II.
needs_review: Verify service chronology and award details with CIA, U.S. military and archival sources.
